after.description: The Eureka J15 Max Ultra is a robot vacuum and mop with SweepExtend and ScrubExtend edge extensions, IntelliView AI 2.0 infrared and FHD vision, and a self-cleaning station. The page advertises 22,000 Pa suction in its feature and comparison content but lists 21,600 Pa in the Product Specs block; this unresolved manufacturer discrepancy is retained rather than silently choosing one value. It publishes a 6,400 mAh battery, up to 360 minutes runtime, 13.94 x 13.98 x 4.33 in robot dimensions and 62 dB(A) in Quiet mopping-only mode. FlexiRazor blades operate at 400 strokes per minute at the dock; this is not travel speed. Standard thresholds up to 3.3 cm and double-layer thresholds up to 4.5 cm are manufacturer test claims. The 14.63 kg weight includes the station, and the 3 L dust bag and 4 L / 3.4 L clean/dirty water tanks belong to the station, so robot weight and robot water-tank volume remain not documented. Adaptive carpet strategies, Pet Area Deep Cleaning and Pet Search are marked as future OTA features on the reviewed page (roadmap); Intelligent Strategizing is in beta and liquid detection requires spills thicker than 1.5 mm. The displayed price is 1,199.99 USD before a checkout promotion. Charging time, cleaning width, hourly area rate and IP rating are not published.

after.description: The Eureka J12 Ultra is a robot vacuum and mop with Duo Detect AI 3D obstacle detection, LiDAR mapping, app schedules and no-go zones. The manufacturer publishes 350 x 342.5 x 107.5 mm robot dimensions, a 412 x 381 x 566 mm base, a 5,200 mAh battery and up to 150 minutes runtime in Quiet mode. The station self-empties dust for a claimed 75 days and washes the mops before drying them with 55 C warm air. The FAQ gives threshold traversal up to 18 mm and entry into furniture spaces wider than 350 mm. The 16.5 kg weight explicitly includes the station and is not robot weight. Exact-model storefront analytics and metadata publish 1,599 AUD, while the extracted product text has no separate price block. The animal-recognition sentence names E10s, so it is not used as a J12 Ultra feature. The reviewed page publishes no suction pressure, charging time, cleaning width, hourly area rate, robot water-tank volume or IP rating.

before.description: RTK+vision mower for 0.25 acre, 140° AI camera detects 150+ obstacles, 30% slopes, 58 dB

after.description: The catalogued Segway Navimow i110N is linked to the US Navimow i110 product page, whose purchase block publishes a 1,099 USD price, 0.25 acre recommended lawn area, EFLS 2.0 RTK and vision positioning, AI-assisted mapping, VisionFence obstacle avoidance, multi-zone app control, slopes up to 30% (17 degrees), 58 dB(A) noise and manually adjustable 2-3.6 in cutting height. The feature content describes 150+ recognized obstacle types, IP66 and Wi-Fi/Bluetooth; anti-theft tracking and 4G require the separately purchased Access+ module. A separate comparison table starts with 0.125 acre and the FAQ names i105, so its dimensions, mass, 60-minute runtime, charging time, hourly capacity and cutting width are not attributed to i110N. The reviewed exact-model content does not establish robot dimensions, robot mass, battery capacity, runtime, charging time, cutting width or hourly area rate. The existing catalog identity is retained; the source uses the US i110 name.

before.description: Triple-fusion NRTK, LiDAR and vision mower detecting 1 cm obstacles.

after.description: The Segway Navimow H210 is the 0.25 acre variant on the H2 series page, priced at 1,799 USD. H2 feature content describes EFLS fusion of solid-state LiDAR, Network RTK and vision, GeoSketch full-color app maps, automatic mapping, Terrain Adapt and electronic stability control for slopes to 45% (24 degrees), and VisionFence recognition of 200+ obstacle types with 0.4 in detection accuracy. The page publishes a 100 W peak mowing motor, six blades, up to 30 zones, IP66 and 60 dB(A) measured without cutting. Network RTK requires regional coverage; its access and necessary cellular data are included, while Connect+ is a separate service advertised with one year free and 32.90 USD annual renewal. Security features include geo-fence alerts, lift alarms, GPS tracking and Apple Find My. The 0.93 acre-per-day efficiency claim and faster-charging claim explicitly use H220 results and are not attributed to H210. No H210 robot dimensions, robot mass, battery capacity, runtime, charging time or cutting width are established in the extracted product content; accessory battery names and laboratory drive speeds are not substituted.

before.description: LiDAR plus vision mower for 0.37 acre, handles 45% slopes.

after.description: The Segway Navimow i2 LiDAR (i215) uses EFLS solid-state LiDAR and vision fusion, GeoSketch app map editing and one-click automatic lawn mapping without boundary wire or an antenna. The i215 FAQ publishes 25.0 x 17.5 x 11.3 in robot dimensions, a 0.37 acre recommended lawn size and a conditional 0.44 acre maximum map limit; these are not hourly area rates. Feature content claims approximately 200,000 LiDAR points per second, 230 ft detection range, VisionFence recognition of 200+ obstacle types with 0.4 in precision, 45% (24 degree) slopes with electronic stability control, a 100 W peak motor and six blades. It advertises up to 20 zones, ride-on edge cutting, 59 dB(A) no-load noise, IP66 and Alexa/Google Home voice control. The displayed sale price is 1,399 USD against a 1,599 USD regular price. Robot mass, battery capacity, runtime, charging time and cutting width are not established in extracted product content. Laboratory drive speed is not a product travel-speed specification, and the shared X430/X450 4G popup is not an i215 service commitment.

before.description: Camera-only wire-free mower for 600 m2, no satellite antenna needed.

after.description: The Worx Landroid Vision M600 (WR206E) is a vision-only robotic mower for lawns up to 600 m2, using a Full HD wide-angle HDR camera and a neural network without a boundary wire, RTK antenna or prior mapping. The manufacturer publishes 626 x 460 x 265 mm product depth/width/height, a 2 Ah Li-Ion PowerShare battery on the 20 V Max platform, 1.5 A charging current, 18 cm cutting width, manual 30-60 mm cutting-height adjustment, 30% maximum slope, 59 dB noise and IPX5 water resistance. The camera frame processing interval is stated as 0.05 seconds, not a travel speed. Weather-adaptive scheduling, a rain sensor, Bluetooth/Wi-Fi, RFID multi-zone management and OTA/USB updates are advertised. Night mowing requires the optional LED headlight and GPS theft tracking requires the optional Find My Landroid module. Robot mass, runtime, charging time, price and hourly mowing rate are not published; neither platform voltage nor charging current establishes those missing values. The exact WR206E technical table specifies manual cutting height despite generic marketing copy about smartphone adjustment.

before.description: 2-in-1 vacuum-mop, 5 PowerDetect sensors, 360° lidar, base self-empties 60 days, washes/dries pad

after.maxRuntime: Up to 2 h (dry mode on hard floors)
after.handType: None; autonomous robot vacuum and mop
after.description: The Shark PowerDetect NeverTouch Pro (RV2820ZE) is a robot vacuum and mop with five PowerDetect cleaning technologies, 360-degree LiDAR and 3D sensor mapping. The base automatically empties debris into a claimed 60-day-capacity bin, refills water for up to 30 days, and washes and dries the mop after cleaning. NeverStuck lifts over obstacles and thresholds; EdgeDetect uses air blasts when vacuuming and extends the mop up to one inch when mopping. The exact RV2820ZE comparison block publishes up to two hours runtime in dry mode on hard floors, while the technical table lists four-hour charging and a 5.7 in cleaning path. The displayed sale price is 549.99 USD versus a 999.99 USD struck-through price. The page also lists 24.82 lb and 17.52 x 17.32 x 21.38 in without separating robot from base; these system-level or ambiguous values are not used as robot weight or robot dimensions. The 0.3 qt dust cup is not a water tank, and 120 V / 650 W product electrical values are not battery capacity. No suction pressure, battery capacity, IP rating, robot water-tank volume or hourly cleaning rate is established. The base filtration claim is 99.97% capture of non-living allergens at 0.3 microns and above, rather than whole-home allergen elimination.
